issues.reason: The structural half stands — "claimed to V" is a to-infinitive control complement and the instruction set says such complements never seal — but the defect half does not: claim is listed among the NON-FACTIVE attitude verbs, whose rule forbids emitting any predication of P at top level, and the prescribed non-finite treatment here would put an unhedged (Or ...) over treat / prevent / diagnose / cure into the KB, asserting more than the text states; the two rules collide and the parse took the branch that asserts nothing false.

Categorical statements: "a property of a plural's members is never predicated of the group symbol ... a bare (Member <group> <prop>) appears only for a property genuinely of the collection itself (its size, its name)", and "specific" is an incidental descriptive modifier that must distribute over the members.

The loss is real — the bare kind symbol reads as statements at large, broader than "that kind of statement" — but it is not a repairable defect: the reviewer's own first gap records that kind-anaphora has no licensed carrier, the bare class symbol is the instruction set's prescribed form for a non-specific / generic object, and removing the Theme or inventing an anaphora head are both barred.

gaps_confirmed: kind-anaphoric "that kind of N" / "this sort of N" — no way to record the anaphoric link back to a previously described kind, and no way to keep the restriction the demonstrative imposes on the bare class symbol

equative / appositive "or" ("55 percent, or 149") — the disjunction section sends every "or" to an inclusive (Or ...) unless an exclusivity cue fires, which would wrongly disjoin two descriptions of one quantity

disjunction over the VERB of an otherwise shared clause ("treat, prevent, diagnose or cure X"): narrowest-scope has no form that varies the event class while sharing one event witness, and wide scope is reserved for clauses that share nothing

plural demonstrative "those" with an antecedent outside the passage — the anonymous-witness defaults cover he / she / it / they only, so the member kind (person vs thing) is unspecified and the parse's person is a world-knowledge stretch
new_gaps: assertive control verbs ("claimed / admitted / professed to V") sit in a direct collision between two stated rules: "a control verb with a to-infinitive never seals" reifies the complement at top level, while "emit no predication of P at top level for a non-factive attitude" forbids exactly that — nothing says which governs, and for claim the two give opposite parses

an indefinite bare plural introduced INSIDE a seal ("specific diseases") does not project by the sealing rule, yet the group + distribution machinery needs the group symbol at top level to carry a distributing modifier; no rule says how a descriptive modifier on a sealed indefinite plural is expressed
repair_summary: Replaced the group-level (Member sk_disease_1 specific) with the distribution rule (Implication (PartOf $x sk_disease_1) (Member $x specific)) at (STV 1.0 0.9), the form the instruction set prescribes for a descriptive modifier on a plural.
notes: The partitive shape (definite superset, SubsetOf, Cardinality 149 beside the un-reduced (Fraction 55 100)), the per-verb role split, the reduced relative on "regulations", and the postposed (Despite <main> <sub>) are all correct and untouched.
